title: How Long Should a Wedding Slideshow Be? The Simple Math
description: How long should a wedding slideshow be? 5 to 8 minutes for a sit-down showing. See photos per minute, photos per song and how to cut 400 photos to 80.
dek: Minutes to photos to songs, by setting, plus a method for cutting a big pile down.
excerpt: A sit-down wedding slideshow should run 5 to 8 minutes. Here is the math: photos per minute and per song, timing per photo, and how to cut 400 photos down to 80.

faq.q: How many pictures should be in a 5-minute slideshow?
faq.a: About 60 at 5 seconds per photo. At 4 seconds you can fit 75, and at 6 seconds about 50. Take off a few for title cards and a closing photo that holds while the music fades, so plan on 55 or so photos for a 5-minute show with one song change.

faq.q: Is a 10-minute wedding slideshow too long?
faq.a: For a reception where everyone stops to watch, usually yes: guides from WeddingWire, The Knot and Wedding Spot range from under 5 minutes to 10 at most. Ten minutes works at a rehearsal dinner with family and close friends, or as a loop during cocktail hour, where guests can wander off and come back. If you have 10 minutes of photos you love, show a 6-minute cut and loop the full version.

faq.q: How long should a rehearsal dinner slideshow be?
faq.a: About 8 to 10 minutes, or two to three songs. The crowd is smaller and knows the people on screen, so it can carry a longer show than a reception. Watch the total program, though: if the speeches already run 30 minutes, trim the slideshow to 6 or 7 minutes so the evening keeps moving.

faq.q: How long should a looping cocktail hour slideshow be?
faq.a: Make it at least 10 to 15 minutes so the repeat isn’t obvious to guests standing nearby. A loop can hold far more photos than a sit-down show, so this is the place for the extras, group shots and photos of guests. Export it without music or with quiet instrumentals so it doesn’t fight the room.

faq.q: How many songs do you need for a 7-minute slideshow?
faq.a: Two songs of about 3½ minutes each. That gives you roughly 84 photos at 5 seconds apiece. Let the change of song mark the change of chapter, such as growing up in the first song and your story together in the second, and fade the first song out over its last 2 or 3 seconds.
